What the host test does and does not show: the code runs the Linux sequences in the right order against a register *model* written from
the same sources (so it shares my reading of them); it never touches VEN registers while the modelled domain is off or protected, never
writes a larb7 register of another port, never writes the display's SMI common, keeps DMA addresses inside 0xD8000000..0xD9000000, and
every wait ends. It does **not** show that the real block behaves like the model.

## Phone test (for the main session; one flash, boot partition only)

Nothing in 0298 runs at boot: a q10hw1 boot must behave exactly like q10ik until command 7 is sent.

    cd gpu/build/autotest && ./flash_q10at.sh ../../hwcodec/build/q10hw1/ui-sched/nord2-ios-metal-q10hw1-ui654fb60dvfs-cap3500-ram3776-sched.img q10hw1
    python3 phone.py wait && python3 phone.py logs /dev/null            # bring the log offset up to date
    R=../../hwcodec/runs/q10hw1; T=../../hwcodec/tools/hwc.py
    python3 $T run $R --upto 0        # 1. read only: SPM, bus protection, CLK_CFG_13. Cannot change anything.
    python3 $T run $R --upto 1        # 2. venc_sel + VEN domain + gates. Then wait 60 s and `phone.py status` (the camera bring-up died 27-44 s after a bad bus-protection release).
    python3 $T run $R --upto 2        # 3. larb7 ports 7-10, encoder reset, register defaults
    python3 $T run $R --no-off        # 4. encode 640x480 Q90, fetch, decode on the PC, PSNR  -> $R/hw.jpg, $R/check.json
    python3 $T run $R --size 1920x1080 --q 2 --no-off
    python3 $T step 4 $R              # 5. domain off again; then 60 s and `phone.py status`

Steps are idempotent (`run` repeats the earlier steps; a domain already on is left on). Every step's kernel lines (`NORD2 JPG:`) are
saved in `$R/NN-stepS.log`. If the phone stops answering after a step, that step's log file name says which one; recovery is the usual
reset to fastboot and q10ik. Success criterion for M1: `check.json` verdict `PASS` (valid markers, right size, PSNR >= 30 dB on all
three planes against the kernel's test picture) **and** the kernel line `status 0x1 … size N`.

What I expect to be uncertain on first contact, in order: (1) whether the done bit shows in INT_STS when the GIC line is not taken (it
should: it is a status register) ; (2) whether larb7 needs the display SMI common's clocks beyond what the running display keeps on;
(3) the `venc_sel` parent (182 MHz chosen conservatively; not a stock measurement); (4) whether the block writes complete JPEG headers
(the checker tells).
